thread:
olivia: Quick RFC follow-up — decommissioning cascade safety protocols. I sketched a pragmatic plan for safely removing the shared-enrichment service without surprising downstream teams. High level: adapter shims + dual-write option + progressive canary + signal-driven rollback. cc @vikram @maria

vikram: This looks sensible. One clarification: can we avoid a heavyweight store migration by keeping a read-side shim that translates calls to the new canonical format? That would reduce migration window but adds runtime overhead. :thinking_face:

maria: Observable-first approach please. We need explicit metrics and SLO gates for each step (errors, p95 latency, fallback rate, model-quality delta). Also add a prompt-regression harness to the checklist. Example flag config I had in mind:

```
feature_flag:
  name: decomm-enrichment-shim
  rollout: 0.01
  fallback: enrichment-v1
  metrics: ["p95_latency", "error_rate", "fallback_rate", "semantic_regressions"]
```

kevin: Cache invalidation is the trickiest part. The enrichment service writes long-lived KV blobs used by runtime. We need a migration strategy: either TTL-based expiry + on-read rehydrate OR synchronous backfill during dual-write. Dual-write doubles cost but keeps reads correct immediately. Suggest: dual-write + background reconciliation for 2 weeks, then switch to TTL purge.

olivia: Good notes. Proposed phased rollout:
- Phase 0: infra + adapter shim + tests (dry run)
- Phase 1: dual-write to new store, 0.01 traffic canary, 48h observation window
- Phase 2: ramp to 10% with automated gating (if any SLO breached -> revert to fallback)
- Phase 3: rollback period + reconciliation + final cutover

Runbook snippet (quick):
```
If error_rate > 1% OR p95_latency > baseline * 1.5 for 2 consecutive windows -> set decomm-enrichment-shim.rollout=0 and notify #oncall
Rollback command: `curl -X POST $FF_SERVICE/toggle?env=prod&flag=decomm-enrichment-shim&value=0`
```

deploy-bot: Canary deployed -> env=staging cohort=1% id=canary-1719654321-1 :rocket:

maria: Also: add semantic regression checks against our canonical prompt-set (small sample) at each ramp. If quality delta > 2% -> automatic hold. We should wire this into Redwood Optimize evals so PMs can see diffs.

vikram: Ownership + timeline? I propose owners: olivia (architecture/product), vikram (runtime), maria (observability/quality), kevin (data/cache). Action items: 1) olivia to draft appendix to RFC with the rollout phases; 2) vikram to prototype adapter shim; 3) kevin to draft migration plan for caches; 4) maria to define metric gates and eval harness.

olivia: I'll draft the appendix today and schedule a short sync Wed 10am. If no objections by EOD Friday we open the alpha window next week. Thanks all — this keeps the cutover low-risk and reversible. :ok_hand:
